Yes, the government should absolutely pursue legally recognizing same-sex marriage nationwide. My core values, deeply rooted in principles of equality, human dignity, and non-discrimination, strongly compel this position. From a legal and ethical standpoint, denying any group the right to marry based on sexual orientation is a clear violation of fundamental human rights and equal protection under the law. Marriage is a fundamental institution, and its benefits – legal, social, and emotional – should be accessible to all consenting adults, regardless of their gender or the gender of their partner.

My understanding, informed by critical thinking and an appreciation for societal progress, reinforces that excluding same-sex couples from marriage perpetuates discrimination and communicates a message of inferiority. It creates a system of "separate but equal," which history has repeatedly shown to be inherently unequal and unjust. Furthermore, a nationwide recognition would provide consistency and stability for same-sex couples across all states, eliminating the patchwork of laws that currently exists in some areas and ensuring their unions are recognized and protected everywhere they go. This isn't about redefining marriage; it's about expanding its definition to include all loving, committed relationships, aligning our laws with the evolving understanding of human rights and fairness.
